findings.title: Scope shows a green S/N and a perfect decode while the log is going to fail (tone level is ignored on screen)
findings.problem: The scope's decode line is the feedback the player trusts most. Its colour and the decoded text are driven by S/N only. The judge also requires the tone level to be at least 50% (SPEC.minLevel). If the player turns a shunt capacitor too far (easy with the drag knob, see the knob finding), the noise and the message both collapse. S/N then rises (34 dB in my run), the S/N reads GREEN, the decoder prints a perfect 'CQ CQ DE PIP', and the panel's 'Signal/noise' row is green. Only one small grey row, 'Tone level 7%', is red. The player presses LOG, which counts a mistake (damage, and the 'No failed decode' star is lost), and gets 'The tone itself is down to 7%…'. This contradicts the screen they just read. It teaches the wrong lesson, that the screen lies, and it punishes trusting the main visual. It breaks DR-31 (displayed values must match the judged state), DR-47 (device state on the device) and DR-42 (the prompt shows '← → Turn the knob', not why).
evidence: src/stations/observatory/station.ts:269-271 (decode colour and text use r.snr only)
src/stations/observatory/station.ts:359 (panel S/N row ok-colour ignores level)
mockups/review5/shots/observatory-play-63-tab-at-bench.jpg (S/N 34.2 dB green, 'CQ CQ DE PIP' clean, Tone level 7%)
tools/observatory-play/04-mouse.mjs log: 'The decode fails: The tone itself is down to 7%'
findings.fix: In station.ts drawScope(), compute `ok = r.snr>=SPEC.reliableSnr && r.level>=SPEC.minLevel && (!j.latch||r.latchOk) && (!j.beacon||r.antenna>=.3)` and colour the decode line from that. When r.level < SPEC.minLevel, print the decode faded with dropped letters, e.g. pass `snr=min(r.snr, dB(r.level/SPEC.minLevel)+SPEC.decodeSnr)` into decoded(), so a weak tone garbles visibly, and draw the TONE bar at the left in red with a 'too quiet' icon. In updatePanel(), mark the Signal/noise row ok only when the level also passes. Apply the same rule in logic.ts decoded(): add a `level` argument and garble when level < SPEC.minLevel.
findings.verify: Add a test to tests/station-observatory.spec.ts: shunt C at 68 µF, rerouted. Expect the scope decode not to equal the message (expose `decodedText` in snapshot()) and the S/N row class to be 'no'. Retake observatory-play-63 (a 68 µF shunt): the decode line must be red or garbled.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it. With a 68 µF shunt C, the cable rerouted and the cart 7.97 m away, the scope reads 'S/N 34.2 dB' in green and decodes a clean 'CQ CQ DE PIP'. The panel's Signal/noise row has class 'ok' (green). LOG then fails with 'The tone itself is down to 7%…' and mistakes goes to 1. In code, drawScope's colour and decoded() use only snr (station.ts:269-271, logic.ts:247-252), while judge fails when level < minLevel (logic.ts:171). It is worse than the finding says: the failing 'Tone level 7%' row is not red. Its class is 'no', and ui.css:225 styles .no in grey (ink-2, measured rgb(74,79,104)); only .bad is red. So nothing on screen is red at all. The only remaining cue is a flatter trace.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-observatory-play-03-shunt68u-scope-crop.jpg (S/N 34.2 dB green, clean CQ CQ DE PIP)
mockups/review5/shots/verify-observatory-play-04-shunt68u-log-fail.jpg (fail toast while the scope still reads clean)
src/ui/ui.css:225 (.no is grey ink-2; .bad is red #c0392b)

findings.fix_correction: Keep the proposed fix, and also emit the 'bad' class (red) rather than 'no' (grey) for failing rows in updatePanel (station.ts:353-360), or restyle .station-panel .build li.no in ui.css:225 to red. Apply the level-based garble only when r.level < SPEC.minLevel. Otherwise a level just above 0.5 would print a garbled decode while LOG rates Reliable.

findings.title: R restarts the whole room outside the bench, but R means 'move the cable' at the bench
findings.problem: At the bench, KeyR is mapped to 'route' (move the receiver cable), and the prompt teaches it as 'R Move the cable'. As soon as Pip stands up (E, Esc, or F, which also stands up), KeyR falls through to the global handler, and that calls location.reload() with no confirmation. A player who has learned 'R = cable' and presses it after standing up, for example to check the cart or the room, loses every logged transmission and the timer. I reproduced it: logged job 1, stood up, pressed R, and the room reloaded at job 0, time 0. This is the opposite of 'retry is cheap and safe'. It breaks DR-22 (the same key means the same verb everywhere) and DR-19 (a key must never wipe progress while the player is trying something).
findings.fix: Remap the bench route key so it doesn't collide. Use KeyC ('cable') or Tab-free KeyG in station.ts:305-306, and update the prompt text at station.ts:375. Separately, make the global restart safe: in game.ts:166, require a hold (KeyR held 0.8 s, with a radial fill on the pause button) or open the pause menu with Restart focused instead of reloading directly. Audit every station key map for keys that mean something else in the room: R, Q, F, Space, Tab.
findings.verify: Play test: sit, log job 1, stand up, tap R. Expect snapshot().station.job === 1 and no reload. Add a Playwright test that presses KeyR once outside the bench and expects the same `performance.timeOrigin` (no navigation).
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it. I sat at the bench without moving the cart, logged job 1 (tier 2), pressed Esc (atBench false), then pressed KeyR. performance.timeOrigin changed (1793799670709 → 1793799674090), and the snapshot after the reload was job 0, time 0. The bench keymap maps KeyR to 'route' (station.ts:306) and the hover prompt teaches 'R Move the cable' (station.ts:375). Outside the bench, game.ts:166 sends KeyR to action('restart'), which is location.reload() at game.ts:178 (the finding says :181). game-ui.ts:119 also flags autostart on R, so the reload drops straight back into play with no confirmation.
findings.fix_correction: Do not remap route to KeyC: KeyC is the global camera recentre (src/ui/game-ui.ts:127) and the action bar shows it. KeyG is already 'ground' at the garage bench (garage/station.ts:331), so it also conflicts in spirit. The core fix is making the global R non-destructive: hold for about 0.8 s, or open pause with Restart focused. The bench route can stay a click on the lever, or move to a key with no room meaning.

findings.title: The room part is a 4-second errand: no cable, no chaos route, no physical bonus (the cable is not the star)
findings.problem: The room has 142 props, three astronomers, a dome, a telescope and a spectrum gallery. The only room verb is one carry: grab the motor cart and drop it at least 4 m from the receiver, about 2–4 s of play. Everything else (three transmissions) happens in a menu-like bench view. There is no draggable cable: game.ts hides and doesn't simulate the rope in station rooms. The receiver cable 'route' is a two-state lever on the bench. There is no room obstacle (`obstacles:[]`), no designed chaos shortcut beyond throwing the cart, and all three bonuses are bench metrics (reliable, elegant, no failed log). Nothing in the room is worth chasing. The noise source for jobs 2 and 3 (the 'dome motor whine') has no physical presence at all. The dome, telescope and gallery are scenery the player never uses. Against AGENTS 4 and 5 this is the biggest fun gap in the room. R4A proposed the 'Noisy Neighbours' redesign (the real cable is the receiver line, plus clip-on cans and whips carried up the mast), and none of it is built. Breaks DR-01, DR-05, DR-10 and DR-26.
evidence: src/game.ts:92,104 (plug/cable hidden, no simulateCable for stations)
src/stations/observatory/station.ts:129-133 (route = lever toggling two fixed tube meshes)
src/stations/observatory/logic.ts:124-125 (dome motor noise has no world object)
findings.fix:
Minimum viable version:
(1) Turn on the real rope in this room. In game.ts:92/104, let a level opt in (`level.cable:true`) and anchor it at the receiver rack (room.ts RX, -3.25,-2.45), with its plug at the bench's RECEIVER jack (0-0.88,1.1,-2.15). Replace the route lever with the rope's actual path: compute `rerouted` from the minimum `segmentDistance` between rope points and the cart and the dome motor (sim/cable.ts), so dragging the cable around the dome pier (solid at room.ts:453) lowers the noise live.
(2) Give the dome motor a body: a red drum on the dome rim at (dx+2.2,1.2,dz) with a spinning fan and sparks while jobs 2 and 3 run (reuse buildMotor()).
(3) Add one chaos bonus to station.ts:88-91, e.g. 'Fling the motor cart into the far corner (≥ 9 m)' or 'Knock the gust-flattened whip upright by throwing something at the mast', and mark its target in the survey.
(4) Add a room spec in tests/station-observatory.spec.ts that solves job 1 by dragging the rope clear (no lever).
findings.verify: snapshot().rope.maxLength > 0 in observatory. A new spec reaches won with the cable dragged around the dome and no `route` act. Survey shot (observatory-play-02) shows the cable from rack to bench.
findings.verify_reason: The code agrees. game.ts:92 hides the plug, target, socket and anchor in station rooms, and game.ts:104 skips simulateCable()/drawCable() for stations. The level has obstacles:[]. Route is a two-state lever that toggles visibility between two fixed tube meshes (station.ts:129-133, :233). All three bonuses are bench metrics (station.ts:88-91). The dome motor noise in jobs 2 and 3 has no world object (logic.ts:124-127 is just a tone list, and buildMotor() is only on the cart). R4A's 'Noisy Neighbours' redesign (mockups/review4/DESIGN_A.md:206-212) is unbuilt. Several line citations are wrong: src/levels/observatory.ts is about 25 lines, so obstacles:[] is at line 22, not :275. room.ts has 111 lines, so :453 etc. do not exist; the dome pier solid is at room.ts:68.
findings.fix_correction: Same direction, with correct anchors: rack RX at room.ts:16/:80, dome pier solid at room.ts:68. Whether the global rope is re-enabled for one station is an architecture choice, because every station hides it (game.ts:92). Gate it behind a per-level flag as proposed, so other stations are unaffected.

findings.title: Win push-in cuts Pip at the frame edge and never shows the dome light-up payoff
findings.problem: On the last LOG, the win camera pushes in on winFocus(), which is the bench table plus 0.5 m, then shifts 2.2 m to the right. Pip, standing at the bench, ends up half outside the left edge: only a hat, a mitt and an overalls strap show. The frame is filled with the bench back, a lamp, boxes and the spectrum wall, and the result card then covers the right half. The room's designed payoff, the dome's stars brightening (dressObservatory lightUp at dx=-6.1, dz=-5.3), is about 6 m to the left and completely off-screen. Large confetti pieces also fly over the scope, covering the 'STARS CLEAR' decode, the one in-game reward text. The ending feels flat, and the player never sees the observatory 'come alive'. Breaks DR-11 (Pip and the working machine in the centre 70%) and AGENTS 2 (show, don't tell).
evidence: src/game.ts:373 (push-in target = winFocus + right*2.2, distance 7, pitch .5)
findings.fix: Let a station override the win focus. Add an optional `winFocus?:T.Vector3` (and `winSide?:number`) to the Station type. For the observatory, return the midpoint between the stand (0,-1.55) and the dome (-6.1,-5.3), about (-3,1.2,-3.4), with the right offset at 0 and a distance of 9, so Pip, the bench and the lit dome all fit inside the left 60% (the result card takes the right). Also open the dome shutter on win: rotate a shutter segment on shellOut and add a vertical light shaft through the slit. Spawn the win confetti above Pip (cheer(game,this,'#ffd66b',{x:stand.x,y:2.4,z:stand.z+1})) instead of over the table.
findings.verify: Retake observatory-play-25/26. Pip's bounding box and the dome both lie inside x∈[0.15,0.6]·width, y∈[0.15,0.85]·height. Add a check in tests/station-observatory.spec.ts that projects player and dome positions (expose them in snapshot) after won.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed in observatory-play-26/27 and in my own result shot. Pip is cut by the left edge and the lit dome (room.ts:67 dx=-6.1,dz=-5.3; lightUp at room.ts:109) is entirely off-frame. The result card covers the right half. The push-in target is winFocus (table + 0.5 m, game.ts:398) shifted 2.2 m right, at distance 7 and pitch .5 (game.ts:373). Two details are overstated. More of Pip shows than 'a hat, a mitt and a strap': the head, a raised arm and the torso are visible, cut at x≈0–250 px. Confetti crosses the scope but does not hide 'STARS CLEAR' in shot 26.
extra_evidence: src/game.ts:350 (win() bursts 90 confetti at level.target = the stand, plus 40 over Pip)
findings.fix_correction: The confetti part of the fix does not work as written. cheer() ignores its `at` argument while game.atBench (shared.ts:12), and the final LOG happens at the bench. The confetti over the scope comes mostly from game.ts:350's win() bursts at level.target (the stand, y=2), not from cheer(). Move or lower those bursts in game.ts win() for stations, or change cheer() to honour `at`. The rest of the fix (a station winFocus override framing the stand and the dome) is fine.

findings.title: Job card shows the wrong current step all bench long if the cart step is skipped
findings.problem: The station accepts logging at the bench without moving the cart, which is forgiving and good: job 1 logs at tier 1 'Decodes' with the cart still beside the receiver. But the job card's current step is the first undone step. A player who sat down first therefore sees 'Roll the noisy motor cart away from the receiver' as the current goal through transmissions 1, 2 and 3, while the station panel (top right) says 'Transmission 2/3: Keep the shutter latch powered'. The two HUD panels disagree about what to do now. The dots show five steps but complete out of order, and the card never names the transmission being worked on. Even in a clean run, the station panel 'TRANSMISSION 1/3 Clean up the garbled message' is visible in the room from t=0 while the card says 'Roll the cart', so two goals are on screen from the start. Breaks DR-42 (the card's current step and the prompt agree) and DR-41 (no duplicated panels).
evidence: mockups/review5/shots/observatory-play-01-start.jpg (card: Roll the cart; panel: Clean up the garbled message)
mockups/review5/shots/observatory-play-32-fail-0.1.jpg (at bench, card still 'Roll the noisy motor cart')
tools/observatory-play/07-chaos-grade.mjs log 'latchfail … card: Roll the noisy motor cart away'
findings.fix: (a) In station.ts:85, mark the cart step done when `this.cartMoved || this.logged.length>0`, so it stops being 'current' once the player has moved on. Alternatively, make ObjectivesHUD pick the last step whose predecessors' `at` is irrelevant, i.e. show the highest-index undone step after any later step is done. (b) Hide the station panel outside the bench (station.ts:352 `this.panel.hidden=!j||!this.active`), since the card already carries the transmission title. (c) Fold the bench step into the first transmission ('Transmission 1: …' with the marker on the bench) to cut the dots from 5 to 4.
findings.verify: Spec: sit at the bench without moving the cart, log job 1. Expect `.objective .cur` to contain 'Transmission 2'. Start shot: only one goal text visible (no .station-panel outside the bench).
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it. I sat at the bench without moving the cart (cartDistance 1.42) and logged job 1 at tier 2. After the step tick flashed, .objective .cur read 'Roll the noisy motor cart away from the receiver' while the panel said 'Transmission 2/3'. objectives.ts:104 picks the first undone step. The panel is also visible in the room from t=0 (panelHidden false at start; station.ts:352 hides it only when there is no job), next to the card's 'Roll the cart'.

findings.title: Key prompt points at the wrong thing in jobs 2 and 3 and after the cart is set down
findings.problem:
The one-line prompt is the only how-to text the rules allow, and here it often names the wrong action.
(1) At the start of job 2 it says '← → Turn the knob' for the shunt capacitor left over from job 1. My sweep shows no shunt-C value can pass job 2: S/N peaks at 12.3 dB at 10 µF, but the tone drops to 44%, below the 50% minimum. The prompt steers the player into a dead end.
(2) At the start of job 3 (the antenna job) the prompt is still '← → Turn the knob'. It stays that way after fitting the 75 cm whip, until the whip is stood up, and never points at the rack or the whip, which are the job's subject.
(3) The scope also stays in SWITCH-ON mode from job 2 into job 3, so the signal spectrum the antenna job needs isn't shown.
(4) In the room, after the cart is set down, the card says 'Sit at the signal bench (E)' while the prompt says 'E Grab the cart', then 'E Grab the chair' (nearest-prop fallback).
In every case the prompt contradicts the card. Breaks DR-42 and DR-19.
evidence: src/stations/observatory/station.ts:199 (log advances job but keeps scopeMode)
src/ui/objectives.ts:70,82-83 (station.prompt returns null off-bench → nearest prop)
mockups/review5/shots/observatory-play-21-log2-gust.jpg (job 3 starts in SWITCH-ON view, prompt 'Turn the knob')
mockups/review5/shots/observatory-play-09-cart-set-down.jpg (card: Sit at bench; prompt: Grab the cart)
findings.fix:
In station.ts prompt():
- For a beacon job with r.antenna<.3, return {key:'Click',text:'Fit a whip'} until a rod other than the start rod is fitted, then {key:'O',text:'Stand the whip up'} when !vertical.
- For a latch job when the series slot is empty, return {key:'1–3',text:'Take a can'} rather than the knob.
- Only offer 'Turn the knob' when turning that knob can change the verdict. Cheap test: does any value of that slot's kind, with the other slot fixed, reach the reliable tier? Use logic.solutions() filtered by slot.
- In act('log') success, reset `this.scopeMode='signal'` and `this.knobSlot=undefined` when the job index advances.
- Off-bench, return {key:'E',text:'Work at the bench'} only near it. Otherwise return null once cartMoved, and make objectives.ts skip the nearest-prop fallback in station rooms when the current step's `at()` is the bench (show nothing; the marker leads).
findings.verify: Extend tests/station-observatory.spec.ts. After log 1, expect `.prompt-pill` not to contain 'Turn the knob'. After log 2, expect snapshot().station.scope==='signal' and the prompt to contain 'whip'. Retake observatory-play-09/16/21.
findings.verify_reason: Subclaims 2, 3 and 4 are confirmed. Shot 21 shows job 3 starting in SWITCH-ON with '← → Turn the knob': the scopeMode is kept (station.ts:199) and the fallback is station.ts:378. Shots 09 and 103 show 'Grab the cart' and 'Grab the bean bag' while the card says 'Sit at the signal bench'. Subclaim 1 is partly wrong. My sweep shows a shunt C alone does decode job 2: 3.3 µF gives S/N 7.1 dB at 83% tone, 4.7 µF 8.8 dB at 72%, 6.8 µF 10.1 dB at 59%, all tier 1 'Decodes'. Only the reliable tier is unreachable (best S/N 11.9 dB at 68 µF, with the tone at 7%). So the knob is not a dead end. It caps the player at tier 1 and costs the Reliable star.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/observatory-play-103-cart-dropped-zoom9.jpg (card 'Sit at the signal bench (E)', prompt 'Grab the bean bag')
findings.fix_correction: Reword subclaim 1: 'no shunt-C value reaches Reliable in job 2'. The 'can this knob reach tier ≥2?' check stays valid; use solutions(job,{cartDistance}) filtered on the other slot.

findings.title: 'Elegant' is a moving target that depends on where the cart landed, so the intended filter loses the star
findings.problem: The elegant tier compares the player's parts cost with cheapest(job,{cartDistance:max(cartDistance,4)}). That uses the cart's actual distance. In the clean spec the cart lands about 7.9 m away, and a 1.5 µF shunt capacitor plus the reroute is the cheapest fix, so it rates Elegant. If the player throws the cart further (the fun move, which landed it 9.7–11.6 m away), the reroute alone passes. The same 1.5 µF fix then logs 'Reliable. Cheaper parts can do it too (cost 0 vs 1)' and the Elegant bonus star is gone. The player did 'more' in the room and gets a worse grade, with a message saying the filter, the lesson of the job, wasn't needed. Nothing on screen says the tier depends on cart distance. This rewards a luck variable, not understanding, and makes job 1's filter optional for anyone who throws hard. Breaks DR-38 (tiers reward understanding, not luck) and DR-02 (chaos never punished).
evidence: tools/observatory-play/08-chaos-grade2.mjs log 'log1 … tier 2 … Cheaper parts can do it too (cost 0 vs 1)' with cartD 9.66
findings.fix: Make the elegant reference fixed per job. Compute `best` with a fixed design distance, cheapest(job,{cartDistance:CART_SAFE}), as station.ts:82 already does for the cost limit, and treat any setup at or below that cost as tier 3. Also cap cartCoupling's benefit: `Math.min(1,1.2/Math.max(.3,Math.min(distance,6)))`. Moving the cart then helps up to 6 m, and the filter stays required for a reliable decode (check that job 1's no-cans reroute at 6 m stays below 12 dB). Add a logic.test.ts case: tier(1.5 µF shunt, rerouted, cartDistance 12) === 3.
findings.verify: src/stations/observatory/logic.test.ts new case. Re-run tools/observatory-play/08-chaos-grade2.mjs: log1 tier must be 3 after a far throw.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced in logic and in game. judge() uses cheapest(job,{cartDistance:max(d,4)}) (logic.ts:178). The 1.5 µF shunt with reroute rates tier 3 at 4, 6 and 7.9 m, but tier 2 at 9.66 and 11.6 m with 'Cheaper parts can do it too (cost 0 vs 1)', because at those distances no cans plus a reroute reaches 12.4 to 14 dB. In game, one cart throw landed it 9.83 m away, the same 1.5 µF + reroute logged tier 2, and the result card lost the Elegant star (tiers [2,3,3]).

findings.title: Chaos with job items wrecks the damage and cost axes (prop dollars mixed with parts credits)
findings.problem: Station limits are {time:360, damage:1, cost:ceil(cheapest×1.25)=12}. The cost axis adds `game.cost`, the prop-damage cost from prefabs: cart 50, chair 25, monitor 130, desk 80. That sits on a scale 20–100× larger than the 1–3 credit filter parts the bench shows as 'Parts cost'. In my chaos run, throwing the motor cart (the room's only fun move, and a valid way to finish step 1), plus one knocked prop, put damage at 2 and cost at 53. That is a D on cost and B on damage. A single chair knocked over gives cost 25+9 = 34, which is C. The overall grade survives only because 'best of three' leans on the generous 360 s time limit. The result card still shows the player red-flagged axes for exactly the slapstick AGENTS 5 says must never be a fail. Failed LOG presses also count as damage (limit 1), so two experiments cost the damage A. Breaks DR-07 (each axis tuned per room), DR-02 (chaos never a failure) and DR-38 (experiments are learning, not damage).
evidence: src/game.ts:335 (prop damage adds prefabs cost to this.cost)
findings.fix: Separate the units in game.ts:353. For station rooms, grade cost on the station's parts credits only (`this.cost = s.cost` and keep prop damage on the damage axis), or scale prop cost into credits (`prefabs.cost/25`). Raise the station damage limit to ~5 so knocking a few props stays A. Count failed LOGs as a separate 'retries' stat shown on the result card, not damage (station.ts:195 `this.mistakes++` feeds damage via score()). Keep the 'No failed decode logged' star as the precision reward.
findings.verify: Re-run 08-chaos-grade2.mjs and read the result card. Cost row ≤ 12 (A) and damage A after one cart throw. Add a grade unit test for the station path.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced. One cart throw with Q, the room's designed chaos move, damaged the cart prop: damage 1, cost +50 (prefabs cart cost 50, added at game.ts:335). Finishing all three jobs cleanly then gave a result card of time A, damage 1 A, cost 59 D (limit ceil(9×1.25)=12, so D above 36). The grade is best of three (grade.ts:6), so the overall grade is still A, but the card flags a D for the slapstick. Station mistakes add to damage at game.ts:353 with limit 1 (station.ts:63), so two failed LOGs make damage a B.

findings.title: Job 2 latch failure and job 3 gust have no world event: failures and twists are sentences or invisible
findings.problem: Job 2's lesson is that a series capacitor blocks the 12 V DC, so the dome-shutter latch drops out. When it fails, nothing happens to the dome. The only cues are a small lamp on the bench going grey and a 2-line toast ('The latch dropped out: a series capacitor passes changes but no steady DC…'). Standing up and surveying the room shows no change at all. The success messages 'DOME OPEN' and 'STARS CLEAR' also have no world consequence until the very end. In job 3, the 'gust over the roof' that lays the whip flat is the twist that should teach polarisation. In practice the fitted whip is the 3.1 cm stub, so going 'flat' is a 1–2 px change. The dust puff is a small cream disc hanging in mid-air in front of the clutter, and the player is never shown that anything happened. Job 3 is then solved by clicking each of four rods and toggling orientation (8 free tries), with no cost and no physical act beyond clicking. R4A asked for the shutter to slam shut and for whips carried up the mast. Breaks DR-28 (failure shows its cause in the world first), DR-37 (hidden rules shown by the world) and DR-26 (concept taught by a physical act).
evidence: src/stations/observatory/station.ts:195 (fail = toast + groan + alarm at table)
src/stations/observatory/station.ts:56 (rodLen: 3.1 cm whip is 0.11 m tall)
mockups/review5/shots/observatory-play-21-log2-gust.jpg (gust: dust disc floating, whip change invisible)
tools/observatory-play/08-chaos-grade2.mjs log rods sweep (r75 up is the only pass; trying all is free)
findings.fix:
(1) Build a dome shutter. Add a curved shutter panel on shellOut (room.ts:456) driven by `latchOk` for latch jobs: it slides open when the latch holds, and slams shut with a thud and a dust ring when the latch drops (call from station.ts update/redraw, and make the room return `shutter(open:boolean)`). Move the latch lamp's meaning into the world: the astronomer at the telescope (-4.4,-4.4) gets the alarm pose when it slams.
(2) Gust: start job 3 with the long 1.5 m whip fitted (rod:'r150' in station.ts:66 or set in gust()), so going flat is a big visible swing. Animate it over 0.4 s (lerp whip.rotation.z) and burst the dust at the whip tip.
(3) Charge a small credit for each rod swap (0.5) or count rod tries, so the elegant tier needs a first-try fit. Show λ/4 on the rack as a ruler graphic rather than requiring trial.
findings.verify: Screenshot pair: series-C latch fail at +0.3 s shows the shutter closing in the room survey. Gust shot shows a visibly flat long whip. Spec: brute-forcing 4 rods costs credits (snapshot().station.spent > 0).
findings.verify_reason: Shot 96 shows the latch failure as a grey lamp plus a toast. The room survey right after (shot 97) shows no change anywhere in the room. In code, the gust only sets vertical=false and bursts 8 dust particles at the mount (station.ts:205). The start rod is 'r3' (station.ts:66), shown 0.11 m tall (rodLen at :56), so laying it flat is a tiny change (shot 21). Rod swaps and orient are free, unlimited acts (station.ts:189-190).
findings.fix_correction: Drop part (3), charging 0.5 credits per rod swap. It punishes experimenting, which conflicts with DR-38 and with this reviewer's own finding 7 (experiments are not damage). If brute force is the concern, make the Elegant tier for job 3 require the right whip on the first fit (count fits, no cost), or show the λ/4 match on the rack. Parts (1) and (2) are fine; the shutter mesh goes on shellOut at room.ts:72, not :456.

findings.title: Knob drag is about 10 px per E6 step, far too twitchy (one flick jumps 100 nF → 68 µF)
findings.problem: Dragging a slotted can's knob is the main continuous control (R4A asked for one). The drag maps world-x on the board plane at 4 cm per step. From the bench camera, 4 cm is about 10 px at 1440×900. A natural 180 px mouse flick moved the shunt capacitor 17 steps, from 100 nF to the 68 µF end stop. That kills the tone and makes the next LOG a mistake. There is no detent feedback beyond a quiet tone, the knob tag text is unreadable (see the tag finding), and arrow keys are the only fine control. On a phone this is worse. Breaks DR-14/DR-18 in spirit (forgiving, non-finicky controls) and DR-22.
evidence: tools/observatory-play/04-mouse.mjs log 'after drag … shunt C 0.000068' after a 180 px drag
findings.fix: Use screen-space pixels instead of board metres. Store clientX at mousedown (add it to Pointer in stations/types.ts) and step every 28 px (`Math.round((e.clientX-x0)/28)`). Alternatively, use 0.12 m per step in station.ts:292. Add a visible detent: scale-pulse the knob and flash the corner line on the scope each step. Clamp to ±1 step per 60 ms to stop flicks skipping the useful range.
findings.verify: Mouse test: a 180 px drag from 100 nF moves at most 6–7 steps (to about 1–1.5 µF). Re-run tools/observatory-play/04-mouse.mjs.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it with real mouse drags on the shunt knob (found by hover at 748,529, from 100 nF each time). 10 px moved 1 step, 20 px 2, 28 px 3, 40 px 4, 90 px reached 3.3 µF, and 180 px reached the 68 µF end stop. That is about 10 px per E6 step, as claimed (station.ts:292 uses 0.04 m per step).

findings.title: Phone portrait: the bench is cropped (no capacitor, no rods) and has no touch controls for the bench keys
findings.problem: At 390×844 the bench camera keeps the desktop framing (distance 6.3, pitch .88) and the bench is about 2× wider than the screen. The capacitor bin and most of the can tray are cut off on the right; the antenna rack is cut off on the left. The capacitor is the job 1 solution, and the whip rack is job 3. The prompt says '← → Turn the knob' and 'S / H Plug it in', but there is no on-screen arrow, Enter (LOG), S or H key. The only alternative is tapping 3D targets that are ~5–10 px wide (rods, knob). In the room, the station panel sits in the middle of the screen over Pip. The survey crops the dome and the right of the gallery. A phone player can't finish job 1 if the capacitor is off-screen. Breaks DR-21 (survey fits on a phone) and DR-22 (controls work in every view).
evidence: src/game.ts:366,370 (fixed survey zoom 44; bench camera ignores aspect)
mockups/review5/shots/observatory-play-83-phone-bench-can.jpg (CAPACITOR off-screen right, rod rack cut left)
findings.fix: In game.ts:370, scale the bench distance by aspect: `d = v.distance * Math.max(1, (16/10)/aspect * .75)`, and on portrait raise the pitch to ~1.1 so the bench is seen from above. Alternatively, give the Station view a `portrait` override ({distance:9.5,pitch:1.15}). Add a bench action strip on touch (`body[data-touch][data-bench]`): ◀ ▶ (turn), LOG, and a 'swap slot' button, wired to station.act('turn'|'log'). Hide .station-panel on phones outside the bench. Make survey zoom fit the room bounds for the aspect (`zoom = max(44, depth/tan(fov/2)/aspect…)`).
findings.verify: Retake observatory-play-80..83 at 390×844. The whole bench (rack to tray) is inside the frame, and a touch-only run completes job 1 (Playwright with hasTouch, tap targets only).
findings.verify_reason: Shot 83 at 390×844 confirms it: the capacitor bin is off-screen right, the coil is cut, the rack is cut left, and there are no touch controls for ←/→, Enter, S or H. No bench touch strip exists in src/ui (ui.css:244-257 only hides the walk controls and moves the panels). In shot 80 the room panel sits over the lower room near Pip. One claim is wrong: the bench camera does not ignore aspect. game.ts:372 multiplies the distance by clamp(1.25/aspect,1,2.1). At aspect 0.46 that clamps at 2.1 (needed about 2.7), so the bench is still too wide. 'Can't finish job 1' is overstated: a far cart throw plus reroute decodes job 1 with no cans (tier 2 beyond about 9.4 m). Job 2's solutions all need the capacitor (L+C), though, so a phone player is still blocked later.
findings.fix_correction: Not 'add aspect scaling', which already exists: raise the clamp's upper bound in game.ts:372 (for example clamp(1.25/aspect,1,3)) and/or add a portrait pitch/lookX override in Station.view. The touch action strip is still needed.

findings.title: Bench HUD carries about 100 words, and every value appears two or three times
findings.fix:
- Cut the panel to three rows that are not shown elsewhere: Motor cart distance (job 1 only), Latch volts (latch jobs), Parts cost. Move Tone level onto the scope as a bar beside TONE ●. Drop the Series, Shunt and Filter rows, since the cans and their tags already show them.

findings.title: F (and Space) at the bench quietly stand Pip up or act; the F button does nothing in this room
findings.problem: The bench keymap handles only 13 keys. Any other key falls through to the room handler. F (the action bar's 'plug' button) runs interact(cableOnly), which, while atBench, calls leaveBench(). Pressing F at the bench (a natural guess for 'plug the can in', given the plug icon) silently stands Pip up and switches to the room camera. Pressing Esc again then opens pause. In the room, F always just shrugs because there is no cable, yet the plug button is always shown. Tab at the bench toggles survey invisibly, leaving survey on after standing up. No bench key (S, H, O, L, T, Backspace, Enter) is listed anywhere: the pause screen's control card shows only room keys. Breaks DR-22 (the same key means the same verb; no key acts unexpectedly) and DR-17 (no false affordance).
evidence: src/game.ts:164 (only station.key() codes are consumed at bench)
mockups/review5/shots/observatory-play-07-holding-cart.jpg (F plug button shown in a cableless room)
findings.fix: In game.ts:164, while atBench swallow every gameplay key that the station doesn't map (F, Q, Space, Tab, R) instead of letting it fall through. Map F to the bench's 'plug into the hovered slot' (station.act('slot',hoveredSlot)) so the plug icon means plug. Hide the F action button in rooms without a cable (`body[data-cable=false] .action-cable{display:none}`). Add a bench key strip to the pause card when g.atBench, generated from station.key's map.
findings.verify: Key matrix script: at the bench press F, Q, Space, Tab and R. atBench stays true and nothing else changes (except F plugging a held can). Pause at the bench lists the bench keys.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it. Pressing KeyF at the bench set atBench to false, because KeyF is not in the station keymap (station.ts:305-306) and falls through game.ts:164 to action('cable'), which runs interact(true) and leaveBench() (game.ts:198). In shot 01 the F plug button is shown in a room with no cable. The Tab-at-bench claim is consistent with code (Tab falls through and toggles this.survey, which updateCamera's bench branch overrides), but I did not reproduce it.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-observatory-play/02-play.mjs output: 'after F at bench atBench= false'

findings.title: Bench hit targets are tiny and several controls have no hover prompt
findings.problem: The whips in the rack are clickable only on the 2.4 cm-diameter rod and the tip ball, about 5–8 px wide on screen. A pointer sweep of the rack box hit a whip on only about 6% of samples. The labelled caption plates ('17 cm', '75 cm') under each whip, which a player naturally clicks, are not clickable. LOG, SIGNAL, SWITCH-ON, SPEAKER and the slots show the pointer cursor, but the prompt keeps saying '1–3 Take a can', so hovering the green LOG button never says 'Enter Log the decode'. Can keys 1–3 and slot keys S/H appear only in the prompt, not on the cans or slots, and 'H' for sHunt is not guessable. Breaks DR-19 (every prompt is the real action at that moment) and DR-44/DR-47 (affordance on the device).
evidence: src/stations/observatory/station.ts:144-145 (click target = rod group: 0.012 m radius rod)
tools/observatory-play/05-rodhit.mjs log 'pointer hits in rack box 118 / 1591 samples, 99 whips'
tools/observatory-play/04-mouse.mjs log (hover log/signal/speaker → '1–3 Take a can')
findings.fix:
- Add an invisible pick box (0.18×0.7×0.16, MeshBasicMaterial visible:false, layers kept for raycast) around each rack whip plus its caption, and register it with this.click(box,'rod',id).
- In prompt(): add hover cases for 'log' → {key:'Enter',text:'Log the decode'}, 'scope' → {key:'T',text:'Switch the scope view'}, 'listen' → {key:'L',text:'Mute or unmute the speaker'}, and 'slot' (empty) → {key:'1–3',text:'Take a can first'}.
- Print small key caps on the bench: '1', '2', '3' on the can bins, and 'S' and 'H' on the SERIES and SHUNT signs. Consider remapping shunt to 'G' (to Ground) to match the GROUND label.
findings.verify: Rerun 05-rodhit.mjs: at least 25% of rack-box samples hit a whip. The hover script shows LOG → 'Enter Log the decode'.
findings.verify_reason: Code-confirmed. Rack whips register only the thin rod group as the click target (station.ts:144-145). The caption signs are not registered (station.ts:147). prompt() has hover cases only for knob, pick, rod, orient and route (station.ts:369-375), so hovering LOG, SIGNAL, SWITCH-ON or SPEAKER falls back to 'Take a can' or 'Turn the knob'. Shot 71 shows thin rods. I did not re-run the reviewer's 6% hit-rate sample.

findings.title: Absurd readouts: '−180.0 dB' and 'Tone level 0%' when the gust lays the whip flat
findings.problem: At the start of job 3, a flat 3.1 cm whip gives an antenna factor of about 1e-37. The panel prints 'Signal/noise −180.0 dB' and 'Tone level 0%'; other rods print −160.2, −140.2 and −42 dB. These numbers are simulation artefacts (the 1e-6 floor in dB()). They mean nothing to a learner and look like a bug. The scope shows 'S/N -180.0 dB' as well. Breaks DR-31 (displayed numbers must be meaningful simulation values at the level taught).
findings.fix: Clamp the antenna factor to a floor of 0.01 (−40 dB) in antennaFactor() (logic.ts:101): `Math.max(.01, …)`. In the panel and scope, show 'no signal' when r.level < 0.05 instead of the S/N number (station.ts:270, :359).
findings.verify: Unit test in logic.test.ts: read(beacon job, r3 flat).snr ≥ −40. Retake observatory-play-21: the panel reads 'no signal'.
findings.verify_reason: Shot 21 shows 'Signal/noise −180.0 dB' and 'Tone level 0%'. My logic sweep for job 3 with 10 mH + 1 µF gives r3 −180 (flat and upright), r17 −160.2 flat and −140.2 upright, r75 −7.8 flat and 12.2 upright, r150 −42/−22. One source detail is wrong: the −180 floor comes from dB()'s 1e-9 clamp (logic.ts:85; 20·log10(1e-9) = −180), not the 1e-6 noise floor at :144.
findings.fix_correction: The fix (antenna factor floor of 0.01 plus 'no signal' when level < 0.05) is fine. Cite logic.ts:85 as the source of −180.

findings.title: Rack and dome shell never fade; the bench camera frames clutter, not the receiver or the cart
findings.problem: The receiver rack (0.9×1.5×0.7 m, navy) with its 3.9 m mast, the dome's outer shell (2.6 m half-sphere) and the telescope pier are not occluders. From back or side orbits they cover Pip: the rack hides Pip's body when Pip stands at the dome rim, and the cream shell back fills a third of the screen when orbiting behind it. The bench camera's top ~40% is filled with clutter behind the bench: stacked boxes left of the scope, a reading lamp poking into the right of the scope, and a chair. The receiver rack (where the signal comes from) and the motor cart (the job 1 lever) are not in frame, so the cause-and-effect link between room and bench is invisible from the bench. The objective marker is a flat, unoutlined pale-yellow cone (~25 px at the game camera) that blends with the brass dome ring and the yellow rack plate. Breaks DR-12 (no mesh > 1.2 m hides Pip), DR-44 (outlined marker ≥ 24 px) and DR-43 (goal is high contrast).
evidence: src/levels/observatory.ts:278-279 (clutter lanes don't keep the bench camera backdrop clear)
findings.fix:
- Register the rack group, the shellOut mesh and the telescope pier with the occluder list used by the camera fade (decor.ts:55 helper), and use the alpha-hash fade.
- Add a clutter exclusion lane for the bench camera's backdrop: in observatory.ts:279, add {points:[[-2.5,-4.2],[2.5,-4.2]],r:1.4} so nothing tall stands directly behind the scope.
- Widen the bench view slightly (lookX -0.6, distance 7) so the rack and the RECEIVER cable entry are in the left of the frame.
- Give the marker an ink outline (outlineParameters visible) and a 2-tone toon material, and scale it ×1.4 in station rooms.
findings.verify: Orbit sweep at zoom 9 and 38 around (-4.9,-3.9): Pip ≥ 70% visible. Bench shot retake: no prop above the scope's top edge, and the rack visible at the left.
findings.verify_reason: Shot 77 shows the navy rack covering Pip's body at the dome rim. The rack, shellOut and telescope are not pushed to game.occluders (room.ts:72 and :80-86; only decor pillars are, decor.ts:55). Shot 63 shows stacked boxes, a chair and a lamp behind and beside the scope, with the rack and the cart not in the bench frame. The marker is an unoutlined MeshBasic cone (objectives.ts:97-98). Several citations are wrong. room.ts has only 111 lines: the rack is at :80-86, not :465-469, and shellOut at :72, not :456. levels/observatory.ts is about 25 lines, so the clutter is at :25, not :278-279.
findings.fix_correction: Use the correct anchors: room.ts:72 (shellOut) and :80-86 (rack), and the clutter config at levels/observatory.ts:25. Registering these as occluders needs a cloned transparent material per mesh, as game.box(fade) does at game.ts:111-113, because the shared toon() materials would fade every mesh using them.

findings.title: 'Roll the cart' is actually a lift: tilted carry clips clutter, and the cart is set down on its end
findings.problem: The step and prompts say 'Roll the noisy motor cart away' and 'Keep rolling it away'. But the cart (mass 8) is picked up like a box and carried at a ~40° tilt in front of Pip. It sweeps through chairs and clutter, and the motor drum and fan sit at Pip's face height. On E it is dropped with its carried orientation, so in two of two runs it landed standing on its end or on its side on a chair. The motor cart also reads small at the game camera: the 'MOTOR' tag isn't readable and the noise sparks are 3 tiny particles every 0.5–1.1 s. A second, decorative violet cart (6.8,4.4) with the same silhouette also prompts 'Grab the cart'. Breaks DR-65 (carried items level in front of the chest), DR-47 (a noisy device should look noisy) and DR-17 (no look-alike false affordance).
evidence: src/stations/observatory/station.ts:316 (3 sparks per 0.5–1.1 s, job 1 only)
findings.fix:
- Give the motor cart a push mode: while held, keep it on its wheels (lock rotation to yaw, y at the rest height) and place it 0.9 m ahead of Pip with the push-bar pose, like the Lunch dolly. On drop, reset the rotation to upright yaw (station.dropped hook → setRotation(yaw only)).
- Raise the motor's readability: an animated buzz (scale jitter 2%), 6–8 bright sparks per second while job 1 runs, and a pulsing ring decal on the floor whose radius equals CART_SAFE (4 m) around the receiver, so 'far enough' is visible.
- Recolour or reshape the decorative cart (a book trolley with books), or remove it.
findings.verify: Carry shot at zoom 9: the cart is upright on its wheels, with no intersection with the head sphere. Drop test: the motor's up-vector y > 0.95 after set-down. Game-camera crop shows sparks and the 4 m ring.
findings.verify_reason: Shot 101 shows the cart carried at about 40°, clipping a chair. In shot 103 it was set down on its end (and shot 09 shows it tipped). Cart mass is 8, under the heavy threshold of 15 (game.ts:332), so it is carried like a box. The wording 'Roll'/'Keep rolling' is at station.ts:85 and :366, and the sparks (3 per 0.5–1.1 s) at station.ts:316. A second decorative cart exists, at levels/observatory.ts:15, not :268.

findings.title: Draw calls about 1,100 at the game camera; survey drops to ~34 fps
findings.problem: snapshot().drawCalls is 1,094 at start, 1,088 in the survey and 839–890 at the bench. That is 4× the DR-24 budget of ≤250, and worse than R3B's 836 for this room, a regression since clutter was added. fps holds at 60 at the game camera on the host GPU, but the Tab survey reported 34 fps. Weaker laptops and phones will stutter in exactly the view used to find the goal. Breaks DR-24.
evidence: tools/observatory-play/01-clean.mjs log 'start … dc:1094', 'survey … fps:34, dc:1088', 'sat … dc:839'
src/stations/observatory/room.ts:467 (27 individual LED spheres in game.root)
findings.fix: Batch static decor: merge the rack LEDs, the light-rail cans, the gallery frames and the bench's static parts into one BufferGeometry per material (BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries, as LR15 did for Lunch). Make sure clutter props use the instanced/batched prop path. Cut duplicate reading lamps from the 'reading' recipe (also a DR-67 variety issue).
findings.verify: snapshot().drawCalls ≤ 250 at start and fps ≥ 50 in the survey on the host GPU (rerun 01-clean.mjs).
findings.verify_reason: The draw-call part is confirmed. In a real-time run without ?manual, snapshot().drawCalls is about 1082–1088 at the game camera and in the survey. That is a regression from R3B's 836, though drawCalls counts every pass including outlines (game.ts:450). The fps part is refuted on the host GPU: the same real-time run holds 60 fps in both the game camera and the survey. The '34 fps in survey' came from ?manual, where advance() blocks the main thread inside the fps window. Also there are 9 rack LED spheres (3×3, room.ts:82-83), not 27.
findings.fix_correction: Drop the survey-fps claim and the 'fps ≥ 50 in survey' verification, which already passes. Keep the draw-call batching (rack LEDs, rail cans, gallery frames, clutter) and verify drawCalls ≤ 250 with a non-manual run such as 06-perf.mjs.

notes.fun:
What works: the room is handsome and cosy. The night dome with the brass telescope, the receiver mast and the spectrum gallery give it a strong identity. Within the first 2 s you can grab a chair and throw it (fastestProp 6.7), and throwing a box at the gallery astronomer gets the '!' alarm (alarmed 1), so DR-03 and DR-04 pass. Throwing the motor cart 9–11 m across the room is a genuinely funny, valid way to finish step 1. At the bench, the Morse trace and the decoded line cleaning up ('CQ ## #E ?IP' → 'CQ CQ DE PIP') is a real toy moment, and the job 2 'ringing at 1 mH, settles at 10 mH' discovery is satisfying.

What hurts: the room is scenery. Its only verb is a 2–4 s cart carry, and then all three jobs are clicks on a bench. There is no cable (AGENTS 4), no designed chaos route or chaos bonus, and the dome, telescope and gallery are never used. Success moments are a toast and a bell. 'DOME OPEN' doesn't open the dome, and the final light-up of the dome stars happens off-screen while the win camera cuts Pip in half. The best physical move (throwing the cart far) is punished twice: it loses the Elegant star through the moving-target tier, and it adds prop dollars to a 12-credit cost limit. A clean scripted solve takes 20 s of game time. The time limit (360 s) is generous, so time is never felt.
notes.playability:
The clean route has no soft-lock. Walks are short (spawn to cart 7 m, cart to bench 6.5 m), so there is no dead walking. Bench-first, wrong parts and failed logs are all recoverable, and a skipped cart step still lets the job finish (forgiving). The key-map hazards are serious:
- R moves the cable at the bench but reloads the room outside it, and that wipes progress (reproduced).
- F at the bench silently stands Pip up.
- Tab at the bench toggles survey invisibly.
- Esc twice pauses.
The knob drag is twitchy (about 10 px per step). The whips are 5–8 px click targets, and their caption plates aren't clickable. LOG, SCOPE and SPEAKER have no hover prompt.
On a 390×844 phone, the bench is cropped: the capacitor and the whip rack are off-screen, and there are no touch buttons for turn/LOG/S/H. The survey crops the room, and the station panel covers Pip.
Other issues: the rack and dome shell don't fade, and they hide Pip at back orbits. Draw calls are about 1,100, and the survey drops to 34 fps. A sprint rampage can shove a heavy desk against the bench front so a straight-line approach stalls (a human can walk around it). The audit reports zero start overlaps, and zero console or page errors in all runs.
notes.clarity:
The start view is readable: the yellow marker sits over the motor cart, there is no prompt at spawn (R3A N1 fixed), and the full room fits the 16:10 survey. But two goals are on screen from t=0: the card says 'Roll the cart' and the station panel says 'Clean up the garbled message'. Several things contradict each other:
- If the cart step is skipped, the card shows 'Roll the noisy motor cart' through all three transmissions.
- Prompts point at the wrong thing: 'Turn the knob' at the start of job 2 (no shunt-C value can pass) and throughout job 3 (the antenna job), and 'Grab the cart' or 'Grab the chair' after the cart is down.
- Most damaging: the scope shows a green S/N and a perfect decode while the tone is at 7%, and the log then fails.
The bench has about 100 words of text plus duplicate values (S/N twice, corner frequency three times). The can tags' corner frequency, the key link between value and frequency, is about 4–5 px. Numbers like '−180.0 dB' read as a bug. The latch lamp and the decoded line are good on-device state cues. The scope's step view with the 'latch needs 9 V' line is clear.
notes.teaching: (Dimension secondary here.) The simulation is honest and the bench now uses real E6 values with a corner-frequency tag and a sweeping scope line, which fixes R4A's 'values can't be reasoned about'. Failure toasts explain the physical cause (a series C passes no DC, a resistor divides the 12 V). But failures don't happen in the world: the latch drop is a grey lamp, and the gust is invisible. Job 3 is free brute force over 4 rods × 2 orientations, which rewards trial over c = fλ, though the RADIO gallery panel (λ ≈ 3 m, 100 MHz) is a nice hidden hint the player never sees from the bench. The 'Elegant' tier depends on how far the cart was thrown.
notes.models: (Dimension secondary here.) The bench is rich: a filter PCB with copper traces, cans with real component tops (resistor bands, coil windings, capacitor can), a brass jack, a whip rack, and a scope cabinet with a live screen. The room props are consistent toon. Issues: the motor cart is carried tilted and lands on its end or on clutter; the marker is unoutlined; the gust dust puff floats mid-air; and the win confetti pieces are fist-sized over the scope screen.

rechecked: R3A N1 (first prompt 'Grab the chair' at spawn): FIXED. No prompt at spawn (observatory-play-01). After the cart is set down, the nearest-prop fallback returns ('Grab the cart' / 'Grab the chair' while the card says Sit at the bench). PARTIAL; filed under the prompt finding.
